issues.legal_issue: A mortgagee’s purchase of mortgaged property at a rent sale does not benefit the mortgagor when the mortgagee’s trifling rent default was not an effective cause of the sale and the mortgagor’s default alone caused it.
material_facts: The mortgaged land formed part of larger holdings, and the mortgagee and mortgagors had agreed to pay specified portions of the rent of those holdings.
The mortgagors repeatedly failed to pay their substantial share of the rent.
The mortgagee paid almost all of the rent it had agreed to pay, leaving only a trifling balance unpaid.
The mortgagee purchased the lands at rent and certificate sales following the rent arrears.
There was no evidence that the mortgagee left the trifling balances unpaid in bad faith or to bring about a sale and purchase by the mortgagee.
issues.conclusion: Section 90 and Illustration (c) of the Indian Trusts Act, 1882 did not apply. The mortgagee’s purchases did not enure for the mortgagors’ benefit, and the sales extinguished the right of redemption.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 90 of the Indian Trusts Act, 1882, a qualified owner who gains an advantage by availing himself of that position, in derogation of others’ rights, must hold the advantage for their benefit. Illustration (c) applies where a mortgagee deliberately allows revenue to fall into arrears so that the land is sold and the mortgagee can purchase it. In Basmat Devi v. Chamru Sao, A.I.R. 1964 S.C. 1707, the mortgagee’s substantial default contributed to the sale, so the purchase benefited the mortgagor. Here, the mortgagee’s trifling default was not a real contributory cause, there was no shown improper purpose, and the mortgagors’ default was the effective cause of the sale; the required advantage gained by availing oneself of the mortgagee’s position was therefore absent.

rule.if: redemption_claim and mortgagee_purchase_at_rent_sale and mortgagor_default_effective_cause and mortgagee_default_trifling and not mortgagee_default_sale_motive

predicates.redemption_claim: The claimant sought redemption of property that had been mortgaged.
predicates.mortgagee_purchase_at_rent_sale: The mortgagee purchased the mortgaged property at a sale following unpaid rent.
predicates.mortgagor_default_effective_cause: The mortgagor failed to pay rent, and that failure was the effective cause of the sale.
predicates.mortgagee_default_trifling: The mortgagee left unpaid only a trifling part of the rent it had agreed to pay.
predicates.mortgagee_default_sale_motive: The mortgagee left rent unpaid in order to bring about a sale and purchase of the property.

issues.definition: When a redemption claim follows a rent-sale purchase by the mortgagee, the mortgagee’s purchase does not benefit the mortgagor and redemption is extinguished if the mortgagor’s default effectively caused the sale, the mortgagee’s own default was trifling, and the mortgagee did not leave rent unpaid to bring about the sale.

issues.legal_issue: A mortgagor cannot redeem only part of the mortgaged property under the right of redemption when a rent sale covered the whole property and extinguished the equity of redemption.
material_facts: The Court proceeded on the footing that the rent sale covered the entire mortgaged lands and that the mortgagee purchased them.
The Court had held that the sale extinguished the mortgagors’ equity of redemption.
The mortgagors relied on the last paragraph of section 60 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 to claim redemption of part of the land on payment of a proportionate part of the mortgage money.
issues.conclusion: The last paragraph of section 60 did not permit partial redemption because the mortgagors no longer owned the equity of redemption in any portion of the lands.
issues.legal_principle: The last paragraph of section 60 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 was inapplicable on the footing that the entire mortgaged property had been sold and purchased at the rent sale. Once that sale extinguished the equity of redemption, there was no remaining equity in a portion of the property that could be redeemed by paying a proportionate amount of the mortgage money.

predicates.redemption_claim: The claimant sought to redeem mortgaged property.
predicates.rent_sale_covers_entire_mortgaged_proper: The rent sale covered the whole mortgaged property, and the purchaser acquired it at that sale.
predicates.sale_extinguishes_redemption_right: The sale extinguished the claimant’s right to redeem the mortgaged property.

issues.definition: A claimant cannot obtain partial redemption when a sale covered the whole mortgaged property and extinguished the right to redeem it.

issues.legal_issue: A partial-redemption decree is maintained on appeal when the respondent did not cross-appeal against that decree, even though the court concludes that the decree should not have been granted.
material_facts: The first appellate court granted redemption of a portion of the mortgaged land.
The High Court affirmed that partial-redemption decree.
The respondent did not file a cross-appeal against the decree.
The Supreme Court concluded that the lower courts should have dismissed the entire redemption suit, but maintained the existing partial-redemption decree in the circumstances.
issues.conclusion: The partial-redemption decree was maintained because the respondent had not cross-appealed against it, and the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: In the circumstances of this appeal, the Court maintained the portion of the decree granting partial redemption because the respondent had filed no cross-appeal against it, notwithstanding the Court’s conclusion that the suit should otherwise have been dismissed in its entirety.

predicates.appeal_challenging_redemption_decree: A party appealed against a decree concerning redemption of mortgaged property.
predicates.lower_court_granted_partial_redemption: A lower court granted redemption of only part of the mortgaged property.
predicates.respondent_filed_no_cross_appeal: The respondent did not file a cross-appeal challenging the partial-redemption decree.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges a redemption decree, a lower court granted redemption of only part of the property, and the respondent filed no cross-appeal, the partial-redemption decree remains in force.
